intent_snapshot.goal: decision-models S6 (application point A16; BR-DEC-6). A maintainer can measure offline how well a decision model classifies revisit candidate chains as avoidable friction, necessary decision, error recovery or unknown. Delegated choices: registry point a16_revisit_chain_class with input_category session_event (non-sensitive); scripts/decision-eval/a16/extract.ts turns a saved revisit --json output (contract immune_brain/revisit_evidence/v2) into one unlabeled row per user_resume chain carrying its pointers and kind fields, preserving gold labels on re-extraction; scripts/decision-eval/a16/run.ts runs through the decision-eval harness with baseline majority_class necessary_decision. The #336 sample (docs/specs/revisit-candidate-triage.spec.md:30) committed only aggregate counts, so tests/fixtures/decision-eval/a16/README.md states the four class definitions from that sample and the corpus is labelled afresh.

acceptance.assertion: In tests/decision-eval-a16.test.ts, extract.ts on a fixture revisit_evidence/v2 output with two user_resume groups (one with two chains) and one repeated_block group emits three rows, one per user_resume chain; an input whose contract is revisit_evidence/v1 exits 1 naming the contract; re-extraction keeps an existing gold label.

In tests/decision-eval-a16.test.ts, run.ts with the fake provider writes a report with the majority_class baseline, per-option metrics and calibration; an unlabeled row is never in a metric denominator.
